newsitem.title: USA: LIFFE locals to trade Bunds at CBOT under linkage.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE locals to trade Bunds at CBOT under linkage.

text.p: A dozen traders from the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange will take up positions in the new German Bund pit at the Chicago Board of Trade when the two exchanges launch their open-outcry link next week, exchange officials said Thursday.
Beginning May 9, German Bund futures and options will trade on the CBOT and U.S. Treasury bond futures and options will trade on LIFFE under the linkage agreement.
About 12 traders from London will relocate to Chicago to participate in pit trading of LIFFE's German Bund contracts on the CBOT floor, said Jack Wigglesworth, LIFFE chairman.

Their role will be to provide liquidity and expertise as trading in LIFFE products gets under way at the CBOT, exchange officials said. Some of the LIFFE "locals," or independent traders, will remain in Chicago permanently. A few CBOT locals also are expected to migrate to the LIFFE floor.

Wigglesworth was in Chicago Thursday to address the annual meeting of the Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce. Both he and CBOT Chairman Patrick Arbor, who also addressed the meeting, emphasized their commitment to open outcry as the preeminent platform for derivatives trading.
The CBOT chairman noted that LIFFE captures 67 percent of total market share in Bund futures, compared with 29 percent for the all-electronic Deutsche Terminboerse in Frankfurt.
"The Chicago Board of Trade will be 150 years old next year," Arbor said. "We will be conducting that open outcry market for the next 150 years."

After linked Bund and bond trading is launched, the two exchanges will follow "reasonably quickly" with a partnership arrangement for 10- and five-year U.S. Treasury notes and U.K. and Italian bonds, Wigglesworth told reporters. He added a date for those links had not been set yet.
Arbor said the first priority was to build Bund volume at the CBOT, which he estimated would initially trade between 5,000 and 15,000 contracts a day.

Pit trading hours for Bund futures and options on the CBOT will be 1020-1400 CDT (1520-1900 GMT) and 1820-2105 CDT (2320-0205 GMT). T-bond derivatives will trade on LIFFE between the hours of 0630-1200 GMT (0130-0700 CDT).

Electronic trading hours on the CBOT's Project A system and LIFFE's APT system are unaffected by the linkage, with both systems continuing to operate under their current schedules, said Yvonne Downs, CBOT senior vice president.
The exchanges amended the link agreement in March to exclude their respective after-hours systems after some Chicago traders objected to plans to restrict electronic trading during link hours.
So far, 69 member firms have arranged link clearing agreements, CBOT figures show.
